The only published coordinates of Uçan Ağıl (north of Sirab, Babek District; 39.291, 45.508, about 17 km from the stored point) come from one source family (Wikipedia/Wikidata); the excavators' papers (Marro, Paléorient 2022; HAL) give no coordinates, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The Wikipedia/Wikidata point (-9.53925, -76.73719) coincides with the centroid of Jacas Grande District in OSM (-9.5400, -76.7371), not with the site; the MINCETUR inventory places Auquin Punta on the Auquin hill above Carhuapata, a 1 km walk from that village (OSM -9.5398, -76.6850), while the stored point lies ~14 km further west. No page prints a site-level coordinate, so there are not two independent sources for the point.

The stored point 48.4559, 28.4200 lies within 0.2 km of the centre of the village of Stina (48.4558, 28.4178 on Wikipedia), not of a Trypillia settlement; the Vinnytsia museum names two excavated settlements near the village (Stina I and Stina IV) and no page prints a point for either, so no two independent sources can be quoted for the site's point.

MINCETUR's inventory puts the temple on the Chilliukani hill between Ollaraya and Unicachi, at km 17 of the Yunguyo-Tinicachi road plus a 0.35 km walk, but prints no coordinates. The Wikidata point lies about 2.5 km from Yunguyo town, inconsistent with that description. Only an OpenStreetMap polygon 'Inti Uyu Pata' (centre about -16.2293, -68.9848, 1.0 km from the stored point in Ollaraya) marks the site itself. Lacking two independent sources for the site's point, it is held for the owner.

The entry names Cappadocia, a historical region of central Anatolia, not a single site; the stored point is the town of Yeşilhisar (Kayseri), and Wikipedia and Wikidata only give a centre for the region (38.62, 34.87 and 38.67, 34.84, some 35-42 km away), so no site point exists to quote and the entry is held for the owner.

The sources disagree by several kilometres: English Wikipedia gives 31.31278, 30.12889 (Pleiades copies it, noting 'Coordinates following GeoHack'), Wikidata 31.304167, 30.100556, the Megalithic Portal 31.4192, 30.1566, and the stored point matches only Atlas Obscura, which the checker cannot read. The excavator's pages (IEASM/Franck Goddio) print no coordinates, so no two independent readable sources give the same point for the submerged city.

The site (per its source page) is the 1866 street fountain on carrer Doctor Palau in the centre of Sant Julià de Lòria; the stored point (42.4505, 1.4512) is the namesake mountain spring 'Font dels Coms' about 3.5 km south-west (a natural spring at 1,739 m in GeoNames and Mapcarta). No page prints the fountain's own point as quotable text, so it cannot be sourced twice.

The entry is the Casma–Sechin culture (Sechin Complex), a spread of ruins over the Casma and Sechin valleys and the coast, not one site; the stored point equals the point Wikipedia gives both the culture article and Sechin Bajo (-9.46472, -78.265), and no independent source gives a point for the culture itself, so the point is held for the owner.

The Maiden Way is a 32 km Roman road from Kirkby Thore to Carvoran; the stored point (English Wikipedia's 54.6250, -2.5609) marks its southern terminus at Kirkby Thore, while Wikidata puts it near Epiacum at mid-route (54.832, -2.474). Both lie on the road, and apart from that one Wikipedia/Wikidata family no source prints coordinates for the road (Roman-road gazetteers give only grid references), so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point is the centre of Isla del Sol, about 4.8 km from the ruins; Spanish Wikipedia (16°02′55″S 69°08′39″O, -16.048638888889, -69.14425) and the OpenStreetMap ruins outline (-16.04868, -69.14421, shown on Mapcarta) agree on the southern-shore site, but outside the Wikipedia family no page prints the point in a quotable coordinate form, so it is held for the owner with that point as the likely value.

Only the Wikidata item of the First Pylon (25.7191, 32.6568) prints the pylon's point in a readable form; Vici.org's entry 'Thebes, Karnak, First Pylon' agrees (25.719046, 32.656757, about 80 m from the stored point) but prints it only as a 'geo:' URI the check cannot read, and the other pages with coordinates (Megalithic Portal) place the whole Temple of Amun, not the pylon, so no second independent quotable source gives the site's point.

The stored point is the summit of the hill (Wikipedia and Wikidata print 52.200, -3.333, so they are the hill's point, not independent evidence for the stone rows on it); for the prehistoric stone rows themselves (Court Stone Row, Cadw RD224, Coflein NPRN 403125) only the Megalithic Portal prints a decimal point (52.203215N 3.335049W, about 0.4 km from the stored point), while Cadw, Coflein and the Heneb HER give only grid references, so no two independent readable sources for the site's point can be quoted.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family gives a point (Wikidata's Hamble Common Camp item 50.8515, -1.3172; the Hamble Common article 50.8525, -1.3175); the pages repeating it (The Great Britain Guide, Wikishire) copy that family, and the independent registers that locate the earthwork (Historic England, Hampshire HER, Atlas of Hillforts) were refused or unreachable, so no second independent source can be quoted.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for Patallacta (English Wikipedia 13°13′53″S 72°25′53″W, 0.18 km from the stored point; Wikidata/Spanish Wikipedia -13.231162, -72.424788, 0.57 km away); the other pages found either copy Wikipedia or print no coordinates, so no second independent quotable point exists.

The stored point lies at the Lefke Gate: Turkish Wikipedia (40°25′44″K 29°43′45″D) and Wikidata (40.42886, 29.72907) put it within about 0.05 km, as do the structured data of Kitabe and Visit Bursa (40.4288241, 29.729072) - but only the Wikimedia family prints the point as visible text, and in Turkish hemisphere letters; no second independent source can be quoted, so the point is held for the owner.

The barrow cemetery lies in the wood west of Kleczanów. OpenStreetMap's node for the NID-registered site (Location: 50.7207640, 21.5492626) and the zabytek.pl map marker (50.7215, 21.5478, not in the page's visible text) both put it about 1.7 km west of the stored point, which is the village centre. That makes only one quotable source for the site's own point; the Wikidata and Wikipedia coordinates are the village's.

English Wikipedia's point for the ruins (9°10'32"S 77°26'00"W) matches the stored point, and the excavator Vega-Centeno (2008) gives the site as UTM 8985250N/232850E (WGS 84), i.e. about -9.1718, -77.4310, 0.5 km away, but a UTM grid reference is not read and no second independent source prints the site's point in degrees, so the point is held for the owner.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family gives a point for Chanhu-daro (26°10'25"N, 68°19'23"E, which the stored point copies); the national register (DOAM), the EFT Sindh survey and the MAFBI excavation reports print no coordinates for the site, and OpenStreetMap maps it only as an outline, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The Wikipedia/Wikidata coordinates are the village's, not the cemetery's. The national register (zabytek.pl, NID) places the registered cemetery at about 54.06848, 18.38933 only in a GPX link, not in visible text, and no second independent source prints the cemetery's own point.
